title: The Limits of American Power
gist: Teaser of William McRaven's essay arguing the Trump administration's war on Iran since February 28 is a glaring case of ignoring the limits of American power, with shifting objectives and a Strait of Hormuz closure that began only after the war started; the text is paywall-truncated.

themes.theme: Iran war and limits of force

insights.claim: The Trump administration's military campaign against Iran since February 28 was launched without a clear rationale and with constantly shifting objectives, from regime change and ending Tehran's nuclear ambitions to reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Unclear war aims raise the odds of prolonged conflict and persistent oil-transit disruption.
insights.quote: The war was launched without a clear rationale and with a constantly shifting set of objectives

insights.claim: The Strait of Hormuz was not closed until the war started, so reopening it became an objective only after the war itself created the closure.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Hormuz disruption is a product of the war, relevant to energy-risk premia.
insights.locator: which wasn't closed until the war started

insights.claim: The author frames the Iran war as a recurring American strategic mistake of recent decades: failing to appreciate the limits of American power.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Expect skepticism of force-based outcomes from establishment military voices.
insights.locator: The war in Iran is far from the first time
